summary: Juan Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Wu completed a PhD at Cardiff University under doctoral supervisor Max Deeg (attested 2012).

Judit Törzsök is an Indologist who earned an MA at Eötvös Loránd University and a DPhil at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, later completing a habilitation under Lyne Bansat-Boudon. Her posts include Lille, CNRS, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2018).

Judith Simmer-Brown is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Cornell College, Florida State, and Walden University (PhD), she taught at institutions including Western Washington University and joined Naropa University in 1977 as Distinguished Professor Emerita.

Juha Pentikäinen is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Helsinki and the University of Turku. He served as Professor of Comparative Religion at the University of Helsinki from circa 1972 to 2008.

Juhn Young Ahn is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of California, Berkeley in 2007. Ahn held a post as Associate Professor of Buddhist and Korean Studies at the University of Michigan (attested 2019).

Juhyung Rhi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and art history/archaeology. Rhi earned a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley and became Professor of Art History at Seoul National University in 1992.
Juichiro Tanabe was a PhD candidate at the University of Bradford from 2000 to 2001 and studied under traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire (1805–1895) worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and Bourbon College, he served as Professor of Greek at the Collège de France from 1838 to 1852.

Jules Bloch (1880–1953) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet, earning degrees from EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. His main posts were at EPHE, INALCO, and the Collège de France (1936–1951).

Jules Brooks Levinson specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins (1994) and served as Assistant Professor of Religion at Hamline University (attested 1996).

Jules Michelet (1798–1874) was a French historian educated at Lycée Charlemagne. He held teaching posts at the École Normale Supérieure, served at the Archives Nationales (1830–1851), and was Professor of History at the Collège de France (1838–1852).

Jules Oppert (1825–1905) worked in linguistics, history, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, completing a PhD at Kiel. He served as professor of Sanskrit at INALCO and as professor of Assyriology at the Collège de France (1874–1905).

Julia A. B. Hegewald is an Indologist and architectural historian. She earned a BA and PhD from SOAS University of London, an MA from the University of Oxford, and completed her habilitation at RWTH Aachen University (1999–2008).

Julia Ching (1934–2001) was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned degrees from the College of New Rochelle, Catholic University of America, and Australian National University, and was appointed professor at the University of Toronto in 1978.

Julia F. Andrews is a scholar of Sinology and art history. She completed studies at Brown University, Harvard University, and the University of California, Berkeley, and took up a post at Ohio State University around 1987.
Julia Leslie (1948–2004) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held an academic post at SOAS University of London from circa 1993 to 2004.

Julian Schott works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. His appointments include positions as a Research Fellow at the University of Hamburg and faculty member at the University of Vienna (both attested 2026).

Julian Strube is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed his habilitation at Heidelberg. He held posts at Heidelberg, Vienna, and Hamburg, before becoming chair of religious studies and intercultural theology at the University of Göttingen in 2024.

Juliane Schober is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed her PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989. She held professorial posts in religious studies at Arizona State University (attested 1997 and 2007).
Julie A. Gifford is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds and held a post at Miami University (attested 2011).
